message.content:
Here are some practical tips to keep your piano in top shape: | Tip | Why it matters | How to do it | |-----|----------------|--------------| | **Keep it at a stable humidity** | Pianos are sensitive to moisture; too dry or too wet can warp wood and affect tuning. | • Use a hygrometer inside the piano.
• Maintain 45‑55 % RH (relative humidity).
• In dry climates, use a humidifier; in damp areas, use a dehumidifier. | | **Tighten the lid properly** | A loose lid can damage the action and cause uneven sound. | • Check the hinges and springs every 6–12 months.
• Tighten screws or replace springs if the lid feels loose. | | **Clean the keys gently** | Dust and grime can dull the keys and interfere with touch. | • Wipe with a soft, dry cloth.
• For sticky keys, use a mild, non‑abrasive cleaner on a cloth (never spray directly). | | **Check the pedals** | Pedals that stick or don’t return can affect performance and damage the mechanism. | • Inspect the pedal springs and cables.
• Adjust or replace as needed. | | **Inspect the strings** | Broken or frayed strings can produce unpleasant sounds and risk injury. | • Look for visible wear or rust.
• Replace any damaged strings promptly. | | **Tune regularly** | Tuning keeps the piano sounding its best and prevents long‑term damage. | • Schedule a professional tuning every 3–6 months (more often in hot/dry climates). | | **Avoid extreme temperatures** | Rapid temperature changes can warp wood and affect tuning stability. | • Keep the piano away from radiators, heaters, or direct sunlight.
• Use a room heater or air conditioner to maintain a consistent temperature. | | **Use a piano cover** | Covers protect against dust, pets, and accidental spills. | • Store the cover when the piano isn’t in use.
• Clean the cover regularly. | | **Check the action** | Loose or worn action parts can affect touch and tone. | • Have a technician inspect the action annually.
• Replace worn components as recommended. | | **Keep it out of reach of pets** | Cats and dogs can scratch or damage the keys and pedals. | • Use a piano guard or keep the piano in a room where pets aren’t allowed. | **Quick Maintenance Checklist (Every 6–12 Months)** 1. Inspect hinges, springs, and screws on the lid. 2. Check the condition of the pedals and their cables. 3. Look for any visible damage to strings or the soundboard. 4. Verify the piano’s humidity level. 5. Schedule a tuning if you haven’t had one in the last 3–6 months. By following these steps, you’ll help preserve the piano’s sound quality, extend its lifespan, and reduce the need for costly repairs. Happy playing!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are some tips to maintain a piano?" They want tips. There's no mention of a specific instrument or city. The user didn't ask for rental prices. So we don't need to call the function. We just answer with tips.
